name: AD8597 / AD8599
tagline: ADI's 1.1 nV/√Hz, −120 dB THD bipolar pair; Head-Fi rollers called the AD8599 'bloody good': dynamic and sparkling.

lineage.note: AD8599 dual first (model by D.F. Bowers, March 2007); AD8597 single added by 2009. No second source.
Enhanced Product AD8599-EP, datasheet Rev. 0 dated 8/15.

part_numbers.note: SOIC-8 only, standard dual pinout, no DIP. Farnell order code 1438872.
Enhanced Product; own datasheet, ±18 V abs. max. Grade differences unchecked.

key_specs.source: Datasheet Rev. F; AD8599 Rev. A

key_specs.value: −120 dB THD at 1 kHz (Rev. F); −105 dB at 20 kHz (Rev. A)
key_specs.source: Datasheet Rev. F; AD8599 Rev. A

key_specs.value: ±4.5 V min, ±15 V typ; ±18 V abs. max
key_specs.condition: SPICE '9/30V' is only a generic label

key_specs.value: Bipolar, likely unity-gain stable; diode input clamp

reputation.summary: Best known from Head-Fi's 'AD8599 is bloody good' thread, where rollers call it dynamic, vivacious, sparkling and 'alive'; another thread finds it warmer than other ADI op-amps. Engineers use it for MDAC volume attenuators, Elecraft KX3/KX2 and T41 SDR I/Q stages, and low-noise instrumentation. Often listed as an OPA1612 / LME49720 alternative. No ASR or Groner measurements.
typical_uses: op-amp rolling in DACs and headphone amps (SOIC-to-DIP adapter)
output amp for MDAC volume attenuators
low-noise line and headphone preamps, low source impedance
SDR I/Q and RX AF preamps (Elecraft KX3/KX2, T41)
precision low-noise instrumentation and ADC drivers
caveats: SOIC-8 only; rolling needs an adapter, whose layout and decoupling affect stability.
Needs at least ±4.5 V rails, ±18 V abs. max; unsuited to low-voltage portable designs.
Low noise helps only at low source impedance; i_n and I_B figures not verified.
Model shows input clamp diodes; check differential input limits before large input steps.
Sound descriptors are subjective forum impressions.

counterfeit_notes: No AD8597/AD8599 counterfeit reports. Sold in SOIC-8/LFCSP via authorised ADI channels, so treat any DIP-8 'AD8599' as a relabel or adapter. Bench check: about 1.1 nV/√Hz and very low THD; a relabelled 5532/4580-class die measures clearly worse.

silicon_changes.identification: Not established. Check the affected-parts lists of PCN 25_0091 and Rev. A; if covered, date codes after Sep 2025 may be Camas-built.
silicon_changes.summary: 'Qualification of ADI Camas Wafer Fab Bipolar Process': Camas, WA fab qualified for ADI bipolar products. Published 6 Jun 2025, effective 8 Sep 2025; Rev. A and a qualification report followed. Confirmed listings are AD711/AD712/AD713; AD8597/AD8599 inclusion unconfirmed.

spec_deltas.before: existing ADI bipolar fab (site not confirmed)

silicon_changes.audio_impact: ADI says same flows, materials and controls, 'ensuring no degradation of quality and reliability performance'. No Camas-part measurements known.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: same process, datasheet unchanged; applicability to AD8597/AD8599 unconfirmed.
silicon_changes.verification: No document links AD8597/AD8599 to PCN 25_0091 or any fab-transfer PCN; neither confirmed nor refuted.

silicon_changes.identification: Date code after the PCN effective date. Die unchanged.
silicon_changes.summary: Package material only: SOIC narrow-body mold compound at Amkor changed to halogen-free. ADI states fit, form, function and reliability are unaffected.
silicon_changes.verification: Scope (halogen-free SOIC-N mold compound at Amkor) matches PCN 10_0004 as described for ADA4898.
